html:
A walled royal city near Agra, in today's Uttar Pradesh, built by the Mughal emperor Akbar from 1571 and his capital until 1585.

Akbar chose the village of Sikri because the Sufi saint Salim Chishti lived there and had foretold the birth of his son, the future Jahangir. The name means "City of Victory"; the huge Buland Darwaza gate marks his conquest of Gujarat. Built quickly in red sandstone, the city mixes Persian, Hindu and Jain forms. It held palaces, a great mosque, the white marble tomb of Salim Chishti, and the Ibadat Khana, where Akbar hosted debates among Muslim, Hindu, Jain, Zoroastrian and Christian scholars, recorded by Abul Fazl.

In 1585 Akbar moved to Lahore to face threats in the northwest, and the court never really returned. A shortage of water is often given as another reason. The city was left nearly intact and empty, which is why it survives so well. It is a World Heritage Site, along with Humayun's Tomb among the great early works of Mughal building. The Chishti order still keeps the saint's shrine.
sum: A walled royal city near Agra, in today's Uttar Pradesh, built by the Mughal emperor Akbar from 1571 and his capital until 1585.
